title: Post-lunch Questioning
subtitle: The first principle is that what you see is real, but it might not be the truth.

trails.title: Confidential Record
trails.description: This document contains confidential information. Please do not take it out of the precinct.

content.text:
Noire, female, arcanist. Her arcane skill allows her to manipulate inanimate objects within a defined range, designating them as "actors."

Born in Hong Kong, in 1950.

Graduated from USC School of Cinematic Arts in 1972. Later worked at what would eventually become known as TVB.

In 1978, she began collaborating with independent production companies to produce low-budget films.

Released her debut film, Muddle, in 1979.

Established New Art Company in 1980 and began working on the film Detective C07.

In 1983, a car accident left her paralyzed from the waist down, allegedly tied to the Film Incident1.

…

1 For more details on the "Film Incident," please refer to the attached documentation.

items.text: Guangfu Restaurant

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Hot damn, rookie. Who coulda guessed the famous director would be a part of her own real-life thriller.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: After talking to her, we still got nothing useful to go on. I can't read anything behind that smiling face of hers.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But if your little theory has got any truth to it, then Noire is in real danger. So, why not talk? Isn't she worried about her own life?

Poitier channels her frustration into her food, devouring most of the meal in the blink of an eye. As she swallows the last shrimp dumpling, she turns to look at Liáng, who is busy chatting with the restaurant owner.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You mean the grocer's daughter has also ...

items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: Yes. So many, many things happening around the neighborhood. Crazy!

items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: But the Lu's are lucky. They took their daughter to a good local doctor, and she got better.

items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: But the other family down the road aren't so lucky. Their grandma was already so weak from arthritis, and now she's gone crazy. She's probably gonna drive them crazy too.

items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: You know what? Another girl, she asked around about this too. *sigh* If I had to guess, it's because of those evil spirits. Things are never easy before the Dùshuò Festival.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Another girl? Do you know who she is?

items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: She said she's an exorcist from the neo-science ... neo-science something ... exorcism office ... and is new here in Chinatown.

items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: She gave me a fancy business card. But I don't know where it is now.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I see. Thank you very much.
As Liáng returns to her seat, Poitier shoots her a questioning look.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: So, any progress?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I have some bad news. First, there are more victims than we expected; second, we're not the only ones who've noticed.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: We need to hurry if we don't want this case to attract wider attention.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Why don't we start with the director, then? She seems like our best lead.
Having cleared the dishes closest to her, Poitier pulls the char siu buns from the other side of the table.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: I've got a hunch her case is connected with this one.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Just like you said, there are too many coincidences to not dig deeper.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: That writer, what was it, Hé Rìjūn? She's an arcanist, right? No surprise that she'd imbue that film with all of her final bits of hatred. I've seen a dozen cases like it.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Cursed objects are weird as heck. It's definitely possible that it could've chased Noire all the way here.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But there isn't any evidence that corroborates the rivalry between Ms. Noire and Ms. Hé.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Hold on. Didn't you read that in a report by another vigil? Maybe it's only hearsay, but that's something.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Not only that. Get this—I did some digging of my own. The night that cleaner leaped off that roof was the exact same night that Noire was in the car accident that left her legs paralyzed.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: It gets freakier. According to the reports, they happened within minutes of each other, and the building was less than a block away from the scene of the accident. How's that for evidence?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: We've got a saying in the DAA, cadet. "When it comes to arcanum, there's no such thing as coincidences."
With this declaration, Poitier pops the last char siu bun into her mouth.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Whether coincidence or not, it isn't much to go on. We need evidence.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Of course. We can't just leap to accusations without proof. But when it comes to arcane crime, you've gotta follow your hunches. So, keep your nose to the ground.
Poitier notices the dejection on Liáng's face and sheepishly sets down her chopsticks.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: I get you. This isn't just about evidence. You don't wanna point the finger at someone you admire.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But you've gotta pursue this, even if that means you have to separate the artist from their work.
Liáng remains silent for a moment, picks up the chilled lemon soda from the table, and takes a sip.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Actually, there is another reason that I'm not entirely convinced that Ms. Noire, the "film incident," and the events in Chinatown are connected.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: In fact, it's quite a substantial reason. If our records are correct, the cursed reel was found and contained by the Foundation six months after the initial incident.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Which means, unless something has gone horribly wrong, it should still be safely stored within the Arcanum Containment Depart—
A sharp crash interrupts her words. The two turn toward the sound.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Oops! I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
A bespectacled girl fumbles with a napkin as she hurriedly tries to clean up the shattered dish she just knocked over.
But her sneaking glances toward the two officers don't escape their attention, and the shiny emblem on her chest tells them exactly where she's from.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Well ...
They exchange a puzzled look.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: If I remember it right, you mentioned earlier that you saw someone from the Foundation acting suspicious yesterday.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Yes, like the lady over there, she also works for the ACD.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Guess we'll have a talk with her.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I agree, Ms. Poitier.
They rise from the table and approach the girl.
Under Liáng and Poitier's relentless questioning, the suspicious Foundation member ultimately surrenders.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Alright, alright. I'll tell.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: But only to you, since you're a vigil, but she isn't, right? Sorry, I should really only disclose this info to other Foundation members.
She shoots a cautious glance at Poitier.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Hmph.
Poitier says nothing, simply raising her chin at Liáng in approval.
Liáng follows the girl out into the empty alley. After verifying Liáng's identity with her communication device, the girl gives a final glance up and down the alley before talking.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: There's no one I would trust more than a vigil, Ms. Liáng.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I'm here on a mission for the Foundation, and you might be able to help me with it.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: September 1990, a female arcanist committed a serious assault and caused a number of casualties. She appeared at an illegal gathering held by the Order of Enlightenment, a subordinate organization of Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: The Timekeeper encountered her and confirmed her identity: Anjo Nala, a Beyond arcanist.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: Born sometime in the 19th century, she was sealed inside a wind-up toy in the year 1968. Since then, she has become a lethal weapon that must obey whoever possesses her toy.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: But back in 1985, I mean, the real 1985 ...

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: That toy had been safely stored in our Arcanum Containment Department as a "dangerous item."

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Until it was stolen.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: You were involved in that particular inventory check. There are four additional items that are now lost aside from No. 066.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: The circumstances of the last "Storm" and that devastating "spell" threw our whole organization into chaos. However, there's no excuse for failing to uphold our department's most crucial mission.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: Fortunately, it appears that our "break-in" was committed by a single culprit.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I heard what you and your partner just said. It's about all the weird things happening in Chinatown, right?

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: It was my mission to catch Latham and retrieve all the arcane objects she'd stolen before they caused more damage.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: But I guess it's already too late for that.
The meaning behind these words is crystal clear. There is no room for Liáng to feign ignorance.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Then you're saying that ...

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Yes, the cursed reel from the incident you mentioned was among the stolen items. And you said that you have some clue about its current whereabouts?
The cursed film reel, Reunion of the Three Swallows, is in Chinatown—The weight of this revelation sinks heavily in Liáng's chest.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I was told to operate under strict secrecy, but at this point, the faster they're retrieved, the better. So, shall we work together?
Scott takes a notebook from her pocket and pulls out a photo tucked inside.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Our main suspect is Latham, an Awakened arcanist.
Liáng can't help but look surprised when she recognizes the other girl in the photograph.
But Scott seems to misinterpret her reaction.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: It's hard for me to believe she'd do this. We were colleagues and close friends. I used to call her Loggerhead, because she's the most forgetful person I know.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: At first, I refused to believe she could do such a thing. I still don't understand why. She's not the kind to be greedy.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: But the Vigiles investigated the theft thoroughly, and the Vigiles are not the kind to make mistakes.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: You've been here a few days already, right? Have you had any word about where she might be?
Scott's brow furrows, her expression torn between hope and fear. It's as if she wants confirmation while equally dreading to hear the truth.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Sorry, I haven't.
She shakes her head.
Scott's expression visibly relaxes.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Oh. What a pity.
